answer: Each identity is bound to a VDF transcript whose state advances through a prescribed chain of modular squarings; each step depends on the previous one. GPUs can run separate clones concurrently, but cannot shorten each clone’s sequential delay, so fabricating many identities requires more elapsed time or hardware. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently; anchor, prism, and lagoon label protocol roles, not shortcuts around the delay.
